def: The French public body responsible for checking that employers comply with employment law, including health and safety rules.

formal.ex: A copy of the internal rules must be filed with the [[labour inspectorate]].
formal.ex_us: A copy of the internal rules must be filed with the [[labor inspectorate]].

everyday.ex: If we ignore this, [[the labour inspectors]] will be at the door within a month.
everyday.ex_us: If we ignore this, [[the labor inspectors]] will be at the door within a month.

collocations: to refer a matter to the inspectorate
the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (US)
note_fr: Il n'existe pas d'inspection généraliste comparable : au Royaume-Uni, la sécurité relève du HSE (ou des collectivités locales) et les autres règles d'organismes distincts ; aux États-Unis, d'OSHA pour la sécurité et d'autres services du Department of Labor pour les salaires et la durée du travail. « Work inspection » est un calque. Orthographe : « labour » (UK), « labor » (US).

explain.written: The inspection du travail is the French labour inspectorate, a state body whose inspectors monitor compliance with the whole of employment law, from working time to health and safety, and may enter any workplace without notice.
explain.spoken: It's the government body that checks employers follow employment law, safety included. Think of it as the HSE and a wage-and-hour regulator rolled into one.

def: An official who visits workplaces to check that employment and safety law is being followed.

formal.ex: The [[labour inspector]] may enter the premises at any time and interview any member of staff.
formal.ex_us: The [[labor inspector]] may enter the premises at any time and interview any member of staff.

everyday.ex: [[The inspector]] wants the working-time records by Friday.

collocations: to show the inspector round (UK) / around (US)
note_fr: Équivalents fonctionnels en matière de sécurité : « HSE inspector » (UK), « OSHA compliance officer » ou « OSHA inspector » (US). L'inspecteur du travail français a toutefois une compétence bien plus large, et faire obstacle à son contrôle est un délit : « obstructing an inspector is a criminal offence ».

def: A visit by an official to check whether a workplace complies with the law.

formal.ex: The site was the subject of an [[unannounced inspection]] on 12 March.
formal.ex_us: The site was the subject of an [[unannounced inspection]] on March 12.

everyday.ex: We had a [[spot check]] from the inspector yesterday, and it went better than I'd feared.
everyday.ex_us: We had a [[surprise inspection]] yesterday, and it went better than I'd feared.

note_fr: Faux ami classique : « to control » = maîtriser, diriger ; contrôler au sens de vérifier se dit « to inspect », « to check », « to audit ». N'écrivez donc pas « the inspector controlled the site ». Inopiné : « unannounced », « without notice ».

term.uk: breach of health and safety regulations

def: A failure to comply with a legal rule on health and safety.

formal.uk: breach of health and safety regulations
formal.ex: The inspector recorded a [[breach of health and safety regulations]] in respect of the unguarded machine.
formal.ex_us: The inspector cited the Company for a [[violation of safety standards]] in respect of the unguarded machine.

everyday.ex: It's a clear [[safety breach]], and we need to deal with it today.
everyday.ex_us: It's a clear [[safety violation]], and we need to deal with it today.

collocations: to be in breach of the regulations
to be cited for a violation (US)
note_fr: « Infraction » existe en anglais mais désigne une entorse mineure. Le Royaume-Uni dit « breach », les États-Unis « violation ». « To be cited » (US) = se voir notifier une infraction ; au Royaume-Uni, l'employeur est « prosecuted » ou reçoit un « notice ». « Offence » (UK) / « offense » (US).

fr: mise en demeure (de l'inspection du travail)
def: A formal document from a safety inspector requiring an employer to put right a breach of the law within a set time.

formal.ex: The Company was served with an [[improvement notice]] requiring it to guard the machine within twenty-one days.
formal.ex_us: The Company was issued a [[citation]] requiring it to guard the machine by the abatement date.

everyday.uk: formal notice to put something right
everyday.ex: We've had a [[formal notice to put it right]], and the clock's ticking.
everyday.ex_us: We've gotten a [[formal notice to fix it]], and the clock's ticking.

collocations: to serve a notice on an employer
to appeal against a notice (UK) / to contest a citation (US)
note_fr: « Improvement notice » est l'outil du HSE britannique ; « citation » celui d'OSHA, généralement assortie d'une amende (« penalty ») et d'un délai de mise en conformité (« abatement date »). Pour la mise en demeure française, dites « formal notice to comply » et expliquez. Faux ami : « citation » ne signifie pas ici une citation littéraire (« quotation »).

fr: arrêt temporaire de travaux ou d'activité
def: An order from an inspector that an activity must stop immediately because it involves a risk of serious injury.

formal.ex: The inspector served a [[prohibition notice]] halting all work on the roof with immediate effect.
formal.ex_us: The inspector issued a [[stop-work order]] halting all work on the roof with immediate effect.

everyday.ex: The inspector has [[shut the roof work down]] until proper edge protection is in place.
everyday.ex_us: The inspector has [[shut the roof work down]] until proper fall protection is in place.

collocations: a risk of serious personal injury
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, l'inspecteur du HSE peut délivrer lui-même une « prohibition notice ». Aux États-Unis, « stop-work order » s'emploie surtout pour les autorités locales ou d'État ; l'OSHA fédérale doit en principe saisir un juge pour faire cesser une activité en cas de danger imminent. En France, l'inspecteur du travail peut ordonner l'arrêt temporaire de certains travaux dangereux.

def: In France, the written document drawn up jointly by a host company and an outside contractor, setting out the risks arising from their working on the same site and the measures to control them.

formal.ex: A [[joint prevention plan]] shall be drawn up with each contractor before any hazardous work begins on the site.

everyday.ex: Has the cleaning company signed the [[contractor safety plan]] yet?

collocations: risks arising from the interaction of activities
note_fr: Dispositif français : inspection commune préalable, puis plan écrit pour les travaux dangereux ou d'une certaine durée. Les Britanniques parleraient de « risk assessments and method statements » (RAMS) exigés du prestataire ; les Américains d'un « contractor safety program ». Entreprise utilisatrice : « host company » ou « client ».

explain.written: Where an outside contractor carries out work on a company's premises, French law requires the two businesses to inspect the site together and, for hazardous or lengthy work, to draw up a written joint prevention plan (plan de prévention) setting out the risks created by their working side by side and the measures agreed to control them.
explain.spoken: When a contractor comes to work on our site, we have to walk round with them first and write down together what could go wrong and who does what about it.

def: A written authorisation that must be obtained before a particularly dangerous task, such as welding or entering a tank, can begin.

formal.ex: No hot work shall be undertaken without a valid [[permit to work]].
formal.ex_us: No hot work shall be performed without a valid [[safe work permit]].

everyday.ex: Have they got a [[permit]] for that welding job?
everyday.ex_us: Do they have a [[permit]] for that welding job?

note_fr: Ambiguïté à lever : « work permit » désigne d'abord l'autorisation de travail d'un étranger. En sécurité, précisez « permit to work » (UK), « hot work permit », « safe work permit ». Permis de feu : « hot work permit ». Espace confiné : « confined space ».

def: The procedure of cutting off and locking a machine's energy sources so that it cannot start while someone is repairing or cleaning it.

formal.ex: Maintenance may begin only once [[isolation and lock-off]] of the equipment has been completed.
formal.ex_us: Maintenance may begin only once [[lockout/tagout]] of the equipment has been completed.

everyday.ex: Did anyone [[lock off]] the conveyor before he went in?
everyday.ex_us: Did anyone [[lock out]] the conveyor before he went in?

collocations: to apply a lock and a tag
note_fr: Faux ami : « consignment » = envoi de marchandises. Le terme américain « lockout/tagout » (LOTO) est connu partout dans l'industrie, y compris au Royaume-Uni, où l'on dit aussi « isolation ». Attention : « isolation » = mise hors énergie ; l'isolation thermique se dit « insulation ».

def: Checks carried out to detect whether an employee is under the influence of drugs or alcohol at work.

formal.ex: [[Drug and alcohol testing]] may be carried out on employees holding safety-critical positions, as provided by the internal rules.
formal.ex_us: [[Drug and alcohol testing]] may be conducted on employees in safety-sensitive positions, as provided by the internal rules.

everyday.ex: They [[breathalyse]] the forklift drivers at random.
everyday.ex_us: They [[breathalyze]] the forklift drivers at random.

note_fr: « Drug » désigne aussi bien un médicament qu'un stupéfiant : le contexte tranche. En France, le dépistage doit être prévu par le règlement intérieur, réservé aux postes où l'état du salarié peut créer un danger, et pouvoir être contesté ; les pratiques américaines sont nettement plus larges. Éthylotest : « breathalyser » (UK), « breathalyzer » (US).
